# Checked for you

These 98 rules apply now, and tooling or an AI review checks them, so you don't need to read them in advance. A failed check names its rule; look it up here.

## Enforced by tooling (52)

### Data and sync (DATA)

**DATA-01** · MUST · Every feature works offline; the network only adds sync and sharing.\
*Verified by:* CI: test suite passes with the network disabled

**DATA-02** · MUST · File formats and schemas carry a version, and every version change ships an automatic, tested migration. Migration tests use real sample files from every released format version. A storage-model change ships an export path back to the previous open format, so no migration strands users.\
*Verified by:* CI: migration tests over the sample-file corpus, one file set per released format version

**DATA-03** · MUST · Writes are crash-safe (atomic replace or journaling): a crash never corrupts saved data.\
*Verified by:* CI: crash-injection test on the write path

### Security (SEC)

**SEC-01** · MUST · `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide (`unsafe_code = "deny"` in the workspace lints). A crate that needs it has an ADR and a crate-root `#![expect(unsafe_code, reason = "ADR-NNNN")]` that CI checks. Every `unsafe` block has a human-written SAFETY comment, is judged sound against the Rust Reference and t-opsem decisions, and runs under Miri (SEC-19). Permit: `unsafe` in FFI crates under the same conditions, with the permit cited in the `expect` reason.\
*Verified by:* CI: workspace lint table (QA-01) with `undocumented_unsafe_blocks`; `expect` reason resolved to an ADR; Miri job

**SEC-02** · MUST · cargo-deny checks every pull request for advisories, licenses and duplicate dependencies, and a daily scheduled scan covers the default branch and every supported release tag (REL-09). A written policy names the advisory severities that block merges and releases. Each deny.toml suppression has a justification and an expiry date. From 1.0, advisories that do not affect the suite get a VEX statement. Clippy's security lints (QA-01) are the project's static analysis, under the same threshold.\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-deny pull-request job and daily scheduled job; suppressions without an expiry fail

**SEC-03** · MUST · No secret enters the repository. A secret scanner the organization runs itself (Betterleaks or an equivalent) checks every push in CI and in a pre-receive or pre-commit hook. A leaked secret is revoked before it is removed from history.\
*Verified by:* CI: secret-scanner job on every push; pre-receive hook on the forge

**SEC-20** · SHOULD · A dependency-update bot runs weekly for Cargo, CI actions and toolchains, groups related crates, and waits at least 7 days after an upstream release except for security fixes. Cargo's native minimum publish age goes into the template once it reaches stable Rust.\
*Verified by:* CI: bot configuration in the template; weekly update pull requests

### Privacy (PRIV)

**PRIV-07** · MUST · Each app keeps a machine-readable data manifest of every endpoint and data flow: data sent, purpose, sensitivity category, default state, retention and review link (PRIV-08). CI fails when code, or an integration test run in a network sandbox, contacts an undeclared host; this gate applies from first release. The privacy notice (PRIV-05) and the store privacy labels (Apple privacy details, Play Data safety, Microsoft privacy URL) are generated from it.\
*Verified by:* CI: manifest schema check; network-sandbox integration test fails on an undeclared host

**PRIV-09** · MUST NOT · An app includes a third-party analytics, advertising, attribution, tracking or crash-reporting SDK. Permit, by ADR: an open-source client for a self-hostable, organization-run endpoint, sending only after the user's PRIV-04 approval.\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-deny ban list

### Accessibility (A11Y)

**A11Y-03** · MUST · Color never carries meaning alone. Design tokens pass WCAG contrast of 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for large text and non-text UI, focus indicators included, checked in the light, dark and high-contrast themes for every registered accent hue (BRAND-01, BRAND-05).\
*Verified by:* CI: contrast test over tokens, per theme and hue

### Internationalization (I18N)

**I18N-03** · MUST · CI runs a pseudo-localized build to catch hard-coded strings and truncation, expanding strings by 50% (I18N-11).\
*Verified by:* CI: pseudo-locale build and screenshot check

**I18N-11** · SHOULD · Sentences are never built from fragments or across several controls. Layouts tolerate text 50% longer than English, and the pseudo-localized build (I18N-03) expands strings to match. Access keys are translated together with their labels.\
*Verified by:* CI: pseudo-locale expansion at 50%; Review checklist: no concatenated strings

### Interface (UX)

**UX-01** · MUST · Visual style comes only from the shared design tokens, in the DTCG 2025.10 format; no hard-coded colors, sizes or fonts.\
*Verified by:* CI: lint for hard-coded colors, sizes and fonts

### Brand (BRAND)

**BRAND-03** · MUST · Every crate published to crates.io is named `kreqo-` followed by one plain word, such as `kreqo-sync`; crates that are never published are exempt. Names are reserved on crates.io as soon as there is code to publish.\
*Verified by:* CI: crate-name check over the workspace's publishable crates

### Performance (PERF)

**PERF-02** · MUST · An idle app uses no CPU: rendering and work are event-driven.\
*Verified by:* CI: idle CPU sample at zero

### Platforms, distribution and updates (PLAT)

**PLAT-01** · MUST · Platforms are tiered: Tier 1 is tested in CI and blocks releases, Tier 2 is built in CI, Tier 3 is best-effort.\
*Verified by:* CI: Tier 1 matrix as required checks

**PLAT-04** · SHOULD · Each repository ships a Nix flake with a development shell and a package; Nix stays optional, and cargo alone builds the project.\
*Verified by:* CI: `nix flake check` and `cargo build` without Nix

### Code quality and testing (QA)

**QA-01** · MUST · Code is formatted with rustfmt and passes Clippy; warnings fail CI. Every crate inherits one lint table: crates in the root workspace through `[lints] workspace = true`, and a nested workspace or a repository outside the monorepo through a generated copy of the root's table, an outside repository's taken from the conventions version it names. CI checks the inheritance and each copy. Suppressions use `#[expect(lint, reason = "…")]`; an `allow` attribute, inner or outer, fails CI. The table enforces SEC-01: `unsafe_code`, `undocumented_unsafe_blocks` and `missing_safety_doc`. Parser, importer and sync crates, which their project's `project.toml` lists, add QA-02's `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic` and `indexing_slicing` as crate-level attributes, which CI checks. Bans for every crate use `disallowed-methods` in the root `clippy.toml`, each with a reason; any other `clippy.toml` repeats them, which CI checks.\
*Verified by:* CI: rustfmt; Clippy with `allow_attributes` and `allow_attributes_without_reason`; an `allow` grep, which also catches the inner attributes Clippy skips; checks that every crate inherits the workspace lints, that each copy matches the root's table, that listed crates carry their attributes, and that every `clippy.toml` repeats the root's bans

**QA-03** · MUST · Core logic has unit and integration tests; invariants such as merges, scheduling and migrations have property-based tests.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo test` and proptest targets

**QA-14** · MUST NOT · Repositories contain generated executables or unreviewable binaries. Binary assets such as fonts, images and test fixtures follow LEGAL-14.\
*Verified by:* CI: binary-file check against the LEGAL-14 directory

**QA-15** · SHOULD · CI fails on unused dependencies (cargo-shear or the `unused_crate_dependencies` lint).\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-shear

**QA-16** · SHOULD · TODO comments reference an issue (`TODO(#123)`), so deferred work stays tracked.\
*Verified by:* CI: TODO lint

### Documentation (DOC)

**DOC-01** · MUST · Every repository has README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, CHANGELOG, LICENSE and CODE\_OF\_CONDUCT files, from the template.\
*Verified by:* CI: required-files check

**DOC-02** · MUST · Public crates set `#![deny(missing_docs)]`. Runnable examples live in the crate's `examples/` folder where they help; a doc example on every item is not required.\
*Verified by:* CI: `missing_docs` lint

**DOC-03** · MUST · Doc tests and the `examples/` directory compile and run in CI.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo test --doc` and `--examples`

**DOC-06** · MUST · An ADR that deviates from a rule declares `deviates: [RULE-ID@version]`, its scope (crates or paths), the reason, the risk and mitigation, and a review-by date. CI lists active deviations and fails when a review date has passed.\
*Verified by:* CI: deviation lister and review-date check

**DOC-11** · MUST · Each published crate's README states its status (stable, experimental, internal, deprecated, placeholder) and maintenance commitment, and is generated from crate-level docs (cargo-rdme), with CI failing on drift. Every published crate package contains its license texts.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo rdme --check`; license files in the package

**DOC-15** · SHOULD · docs.rs builds every crate with all features and shows feature gates; each Cargo feature is documented in the crate docs and in Cargo.toml.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo doc --all-features` with `doc_cfg`

### Versioning and releases (REL)

**REL-01** · MUST · Every public interface follows Semantic Versioning: crate APIs, CLI flags, file formats, the sync protocol, the plugin API, design tokens (names and meanings) and component APIs. *Breaking* for crate APIs follows the [Cargo SemVer chapter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/semver.html); a possibly-breaking change needs a maintainer decision recorded in the PR. Token diffs appear in the changelog. Apps also follow a time-based cadence (REL-10).\
*Verified by:* cargo-semver-checks; token diff job

**REL-02** · MUST · cargo-semver-checks runs on every pull request to a library crate.\
*Verified by:* cargo-semver-checks

**REL-03** · MUST · Pull-request titles follow Conventional Commits and become the subjects of the squash commits on the default branch (CI-13); CI lints them. Subjects describe the change as users would see it, fixes reference their issue, and performance claims cite measurements. Changelogs are generated in the Keep a Changelog format; the generated changelog feeds the curated release notes (REL-13) and never replaces them.\
*Verified by:* CI: pull-request title lint; git-cliff

**REL-04** · MUST · Each crate declares its MSRV, which follows a stated window (for example latest stable minus two). Workspaces use resolver 3. An MSRV job checks publishable crates with the committed lockfile, and each changelog release section states its MSRV. Raising the MSRV is a minor version bump.\
*Verified by:* MSRV job with `--locked`

**REL-14** · MUST · A PR that breaks a public interface adds a migration-guide fragment: what changed, why, how to migrate, a before/after example and searchable names. A PR with a user-visible feature adds a release-note fragment. CI validates fragments, and a deprecation attribute never replaces one.\
*Verified by:* Fragment validation job

### Repository and CI (CI)

**CI-01** · MUST · The default branch is protected: no direct pushes, changes land through pull requests, and force-pushing to or deleting protected branches and release tags is blocked. History is rewritten only through a documented expunging process that two maintainers approve. New collaborators start with read access.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: branch and tag protection; default collaborator role

**CI-02** · MUST · Every pull request passes all required checks (format, lint, tests, cargo-deny, semver, docs) before merge.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: required checks list

**CI-04** · MUST · Tier 1 platforms build and test on every pull request; Tier 2 platforms build nightly.\
*Verified by:* Platform matrix job

**CI-07** · MUST · Workflow steps reference actions by fully qualified URL and full commit SHA, with the version as a comment, and container images by digest.\
*Verified by:* Pin check in the workflow analyzer (CI-09)

**CI-08** · MUST · Every workflow runs with the least privilege it needs: read-only or no permissions by default, writes granted per job, and checkouts never persist credentials. Where the forge lacks per-workflow permissions, the same outcome is enforced through repository settings and scoped tokens.\
*Verified by:* Workflow analyzer: permissions block; credentials not persisted

**CI-09** · MUST · Workflows never run untrusted PR code with secrets or write tokens: no privileged-trigger checkout of the PR head. Untrusted event data (titles, branch names, commit messages) reaches scripts only through environment variables. CI configuration is linted by a workflow analyzer (zizmor where it covers the forge's syntax).\
*Verified by:* zizmor or an equivalent workflow analyzer

**CI-10** · MUST · Runners for PR or untrusted code are ephemeral and isolated in a container or VM: no host runners, no privileged containers, no host networking or Docker socket, no access to internal services. Workflows from non-members need a maintainer's approval to run. Release jobs run on separate dedicated runners that never run PR code.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: runner labels and isolation; approval for outside workflows

**CI-12** · MUST · Every PR uses the template: problem and linked issue or RFC; solution and alternatives; how it was tested, including platforms tested and not tested; risks and compatibility impact; docs updated or not needed; how AI was used (GOV-03); before/after screenshots for UI changes. The description becomes the squash-commit body, and CI checks that the sections are filled in. Details: CONTRIBUTING.md and the template.\
*Verified by:* PR template section check

**CI-13** · MUST · Each PR covers one topic: refactors and cleanups never mix with behavior changes. PRs are squash-merged only, with the forge's squash message set to the PR title and description (CI-12, REL-03), so branch commits stay scaffolding and every commit on the default branch builds and passes CI.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: squash merge is the only merge method, with the title-and-description message; Review checklist: single topic

**CI-16** · MUST · CI and release builds use a pinned Rust toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml`), bumped by deliberate PRs that fix new lints. Every workspace commits `Cargo.lock`, and CI, release and install instructions use `--locked`.\
*Verified by:* `--locked` in workflows; toolchain file present

**CI-17** · MUST · Each package builds and passes Clippy for every feature on its own and with no default features (`cargo hack --each-feature`) on every PR, with `--feature-powerset --depth 2` on a schedule. Crates targeting the web also get a wasm32 check on every PR.\
*Verified by:* cargo-hack job; wasm32 check job

**CI-18** · MUST · AI reviews run from a separate, clearly labeled bot identity and name the model that ran them. While there is one maintainer, an independent AI review counts as the review CI-03 requires, and a finding it marks as blocking holds the merge until it is fixed or the founder dismisses it with a reason.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: bot identity labeled; CI: blocking findings fixed or dismissed with a reason

**CI-19** · SHOULD · CI runs a spell checker (typos) with a project dictionary and one English variant, skipping translations; Taplo for TOML formatting; markdownlint; and freshness checks on generated feature and example indexes.\
*Verified by:* typos, Taplo, markdownlint and freshness jobs

### Governance and contribution (GOV)

**GOV-07** · MUST · GOVERNANCE.md states the decision model (GOV-09); who holds each decision right (RFC sign-off, releases, merges per area); who holds each sensitive access (forge admin, CI secrets, signing keys, registry ownership, DNS); how people join and leave each role; the escalation path (REV-04); and the module that owns the interface guidelines, tokens and component library. Names live only in GOVERNANCE.md; other documents link to it.\
*Verified by:* CI: GOVERNANCE.md present with required sections

**GOV-16** · MUST · Only humans appear in the git author field, and only humans or the forge's merge identity in the committer field. AI tools appear only in the `Co-Authored-By` disclosure trailer (GOV-03) and never as a committer, account or reviewer of record. CI rejects commits that break this.\
*Verified by:* CI: author and committer fields checked against the contributor list and the forge identity

### Licensing and compliance (LEGAL)

**LEGAL-01** · MUST · Licenses follow three groups. An app's own crates (its core and UI shell) are GPL-3.0-or-later; servers and hosted services are AGPL-3.0-or-later; file formats, protocols, algorithms, shared libraries, tools, and the plugin interface and SDK are MIT OR Apache-2.0. Before the first outside contribution, the GPL and AGPL texts carry additional permissions under their section 7, drafted with legal counsel: distribution through app stores whose terms add restrictions, linking the UI toolkit under its non-GPL license, and combining an app with OSI-licensed plugins that use only the published plugin interface (EXT-05). Any other license needs an ADR.\
*Verified by:* CI: each crate's license field matches its group; Review checklist: group of a new crate

**LEGAL-02** · MUST · Every file carries an SPDX license header, following the REUSE specification.\
*Verified by:* `reuse lint`

**LEGAL-03** · MUST · Dependency licenses are compatible with the project's license, enforced by cargo-deny.\
*Verified by:* cargo-deny `licenses`

### Lifecycle and continuity (LIFE)

**LIFE-01** · MUST · Every repository declares its stage in machine-readable metadata (incubating, in review, stable, unmaintained, archived), beside its declared conventions version, and in its README. Only stable projects publish stable-channel releases or carry the Kreqo name. Any stage can move to unmaintained, and an unmaintained project returns to incubating when someone takes it on.\
*Verified by:* CI: stage file present and valid; README badge generated from it

## Checked by AI review (46)

### Architecture (ARCH)

**ARCH-01** · MUST · All logic is written in Rust. Other languages appear only where a platform, format or tool requires them (shaders, markup and styles, translations, design tokens, interface definitions, CI and packaging files, mobile glue) and never hold business logic.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no business logic outside Rust

**ARCH-02** · MUST · Domain logic lives in UI-independent crates; UI crates contain presentation only.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: core crates have no UI dependency; UI crates hold no domain logic

**ARCH-04** · MUST · Each concept (type, rule, constant) is defined once and imported everywhere else.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no duplicated type, rule or constant

**ARCH-06** · MUST · Project scripts and build tasks are written in Rust (cargo xtask), not shell. CI workflow files, packaging manifests and Nix flakes (PLAT-04) are outside this rule and follow ARCH-01.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new automation lives in the xtask crate

**ARCH-07** · SHOULD · Shared code moves into its own crate on its third use, not before. UI patterns follow UX-02 instead.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: extraction justified by three call sites, or by UX-02 for a UI pattern

**ARCH-08** · SHOULD · Crates are small and single-purpose, with optional functionality behind Cargo features.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: one purpose per crate; optional code behind a feature

**ARCH-09** · SHOULD · Configuration, UI descriptions and content specs are declarative where the domain allows.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new config or spec is data, not code

**ARCH-10** · SHOULD · Declarative specs compile to their output ahead of time. Runtime code generation needs an ADR and never ships on iOS.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: ADR linked for any runtime code generation; iOS build excludes it

**ARCH-15** · SHOULD · Code stays plain enough to review in a web diff. New proc-macros, heavy generic or trait machinery, or async in core crates need an ADR. Changes match the surrounding style and never add a second way to do what the codebase already does one way.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no new macro, generic machinery or core async without an ADR; one way per thing

**ARCH-17** · SHOULD · Code promoted into a shared crate first meets the library bar: docs (DOC-02), tests, the workspace lints, a compatible license, and minimal `unsafe` and dependencies.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: library bar items ticked on the promotion PR

### Security (SEC)

**SEC-05** · MUST · Projects meet OSPS Baseline v2026.08.28, re-pinned deliberately on each Baseline release: Level 1 on Day one, Level 2 by first release, Level 3 by 1.0. Evidence is published through the Best Practices badge's Baseline levels or a Security Insights file. The practices behind Scorecard's checks are enforced by forge-neutral tools (CI-07 to CI-10, QA-14, SEC-20); a Scorecard score is not a target.\
*Verified by:* Release checklist: Baseline level evidence (badge or Security Insights file)

### Privacy (PRIV)

**PRIV-01** · MUST · Telemetry and analytics are off by default and run only after explicit opt-in. Telemetry means any measurement that leaves the device: analytics, attribution, experiments, usage pings, diagnostics. Data kept only on the device and visible to the user is not telemetry.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no measurement leaves the device without opt-in; PRIV-07 manifest entry

**PRIV-02** · MUST NOT · Logs, crash reports, bug reports and diagnostic bundles contain secrets, or note, card or file content, titles or paths, unless the user adds them in the preview (PRIV-04).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: redaction of content, titles and paths in logs and bundles

**PRIV-03** · MUST · Apps contact only servers the user chose. A chosen server means the user turned on the feature or started the action, and the host is named in the UI and in the privacy notice. Nothing is contacted because the app launched. On-demand downloads (dictionaries, models, fonts, the plugin directory) follow the same rule, and lookups send the minimum, not library contents.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: every host in the PRIV-07 manifest with its triggering action; nothing on launch

**PRIV-06** · MUST · Every privacy-affecting setting ships at its most protective value. Sharing, sync, public profiles and diagnostics stay off until the user turns them on, and no update switches on a new data flow.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new settings default to their protective value; no data flow enabled by an update

### Accessibility (A11Y)

**A11Y-01** · MUST · Every control exposes a role, a name and a state to screen readers. Icon-only controls carry an accessible name and a tooltip (UX-23); a shortened label exposes its full text as the accessible name; a disabled control exposes why it is disabled; no label repeats within a window.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: accessibility-tree inspection; no duplicate labels

**A11Y-02** · MUST · Every action works from the keyboard, with visible focus and documented shortcuts. Focus looks different from selection, and focus returns to its origin when a dialog closes.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: keyboard-only pass; focus return after dialogs

### Internationalization (I18N)

**I18N-02** · MUST · Dates, numbers, plurals, units and sorting use ICU4X with the user's locale.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: formatting through ICU4X only

### Interface (UX)

**UX-02** · MUST · Every app is built from the suite's component library and bundled fonts, so it looks the same on every platform. New patterns are proposed to the library before they ship, may incubate in one app with Experimental status (UX-20), and are promoted when a second app needs them.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: library components only; incubating patterns marked Experimental

**UX-05** · MUST NOT · Apps use dark patterns: streaks that punish missed days, fake urgency, nagging or hidden cancelation.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no dark patterns

**UX-06** · MUST · Terminology follows the shared glossary in every app and language (I18N-10).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: glossary terms; Weblate consistency check (I18N-10)

**UX-07** · MUST · Error messages say what happened and what to do next, in plain language (UX-15, UX-26).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: errors name the cause and the action

**UX-21** · MUST · The interface never blocks: long work runs in the background with progress and instant cancel, and no dialog asks for input before an action that has a sensible default.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: long operations cancellable; no pre-action dialogs

**UX-25** · MUST NOT · Apps carry third-party advertising or promote cryptocurrencies or related services.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no ads or cryptocurrency promotion

### Performance (PERF)

**PERF-03** · MUST · Data already on the device shows without waiting for the network: no spinners for local data.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: local reads never await the network

### Platforms, distribution and updates (PLAT)

**PLAT-02** · MUST · Linux is Tier 1 for every app, and each app is at its best on Linux.\
*Verified by:* Release checklist: Linux build verified first

### Code quality and testing (QA)

**QA-02** · MUST · Libraries return typed errors and never panic on bad input; apps never crash on a recoverable error.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: error types, no panics on input

**QA-04** · MUST · Logging uses `tracing`, with structured, local, rotating logs.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: `tracing` only, rotation configured

**QA-05** · SHOULD · Public crate APIs follow the Rust API Guidelines.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: API guidelines checklist

**QA-09** · MUST · New functionality ships with tests, and every bug fix adds a test that fails without it, in the same pull request, unless the pull request explains why it cannot. While the default branch fails CI, only changes that fix it merge.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: tests in the same PR, or a stated reason

### Documentation (DOC)

**DOC-04** · MUST · ADRs live in `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md`, numbered sequentially and never reused, using the MADR 4 minimal template plus a Confirmation section. Each opens with a Y-statement (in the context of…, facing…, we decided…, to achieve…, accepting…). Status is proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated or superseded by ADR-NNNN. An accepted ADR is never rewritten except to change its status. Deviation ADRs carry machine-readable front matter (DOC-06).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: template, number, status, Y-statement

**DOC-13** · MUST · Agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) only summarize human-facing docs; no rule or process exists only there.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: agent files cite the human-facing source

### Repository and CI (CI)

**CI-05** · MUST · CI workflows come from the template and follow its updates.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: workflow matches the template version

**CI-14** · SHOULD · A merged change that breaks the default branch or a release is reverted first, then re-landed with a regression test. Its author and reviewer are notified.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: revert PR links the regression test

### Code review (REV)

**REV-01** · MUST · A reviewer approves a change once it clearly improves the codebase and meets every applicable MUST in this document. Perfection is not a merge criterion; further polish goes into a follow-up issue.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: approval states what improved; follow-ups filed

**REV-02** · SHOULD · Reviews follow an order: is the PR valid, is the problem real, does the approach fit, does it work, then the code itself. Every review ends with a summary of what was checked and what couldn't be. Comments use Conventional Comments labels, and only `issue`, `todo` or `(blocking)` comments block a merge. Reviewers never block on personal preference or on style these conventions don't set, and never widen a PR's scope. Details: CONTRIBUTING.md.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: summary present; blocking comments labeled

**REV-04** · MUST · Review disagreements are settled by data first, then by this document, then by the area owner, then by the decision-maker named in GOVERNANCE.md. A design dispute becomes an RFC, and the decision and its reason are recorded on the PR.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: decision recorded on the PR

### Governance and contribution (GOV)

**GOV-03** · MUST · AI assistance is disclosed. Every commit in which AI produced anything beyond single-line completion carries the `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming the model, as emitted by the tooling, and the squash commit keeps every such trailer from the branch (CI-13). The pull request says how AI was used, what it produced, what the human verified, and the human creative input (design, selection, editing). Disclosure covers code, docs, RFCs, ADRs, issues and review comments.\
*Verified by:* CI: squash commit carries the branch's trailers; Review checklist: disclosure block present

**GOV-06** · MUST · The code of conduct is [Contributor Covenant 3.0](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/3/0/code_of_conduct/), with a private reporting address; GOV-21 completes its reporting section before the project opens to outside contributions. Its scope covers the forge, chat, forum and events; app names, descriptions, screenshots and bundled content; and content an AI agent posts under a person's name.\
*Verified by:* CI: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md from the template; Review checklist

**GOV-17** · MUST · AI-created code meets a higher test bar: every edge case the author or reviewer can name is tested, and no untested path merges. Generated code that isn't an extension or refactor of existing project code gets a provenance check (LEGAL-11) before merging.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: edge cases listed and tested; coverage diff on the PR

**GOV-25** · SHOULD NOT · The organization ships model-generated functional media, such as UI icons or placeholder images. Any that ships is revised by a human, disclosed per file in REUSE metadata and license-checked.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: provenance, disclosure and license check per file

**GOV-26** · MUST · Procedural media, generated by a reviewable algorithm whose parameters are in the repository, is not model-generated media, whoever wrote the code. Its code is reviewed like any other (GOV-02, GOV-17), and its output is checked not to reproduce another work. Coordinates or samples a model writes directly, such as SVG path data, count as model-generated media.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: generator in the repository; output provenance check

### Licensing and compliance (LEGAL)

**LEGAL-09** · MUST NOT · An AI system is named as author or co-author in copyright notices, AUTHORS files or copyright registrations. Commit trailers (GOV-03) are not author fields.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no AI in notices or AUTHORS

**LEGAL-11** · MUST · Code copied from elsewhere, including AI output that reproduces it, keeps its license and attribution and is compatible with the target artifact; Anki is AGPL-3.0-or-later, so its code never enters permissive crates. Contributors never copy from, or consult, source-available or proprietary implementations of formats the suite imports; interoperability is built from public specifications and sample files.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: provenance of new code (GOV-17)

**LEGAL-14** · MUST · Every asset is committed in, or next to, its preferred modifiable form (SVG or design source for icons and logos, token sources for generated styles), with instructions to regenerate it. Binary assets (fonts, images, test fixtures) live in a declared directory with provenance notes.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: source form and provenance for every new asset

### Lifecycle and continuity (LIFE)

**LIFE-07** · MUST · The organization publishes the list of its official repositories, on kreqo.org and in the template.\
*Verified by:* CI: repository list generated and published
